title.narrative: KOSOVO: COMPETITIVENESS AND EXPORT READINESS PROJECT

description.narrative: The objective of the Competitiveness and Export Readiness Project for Kosovo is to support product certification for export markets, strengthen the capacity of export-oriented firms and reduce the cost of business inspections. There are two components to the project, the first component being enhancing business environment and export readiness. Component one will contribute to the government's efforts to enhance the business environment and export readiness of firms by modernizing the National Quality Infrastructure, supporting SMEs with export potential, and reforming the business inspections system. This component will finance the following three subcomponents: (i) improving NQI and supporting its international recognition, (ii) supporting businesses to improve export readiness, and (iii) reforming the business inspections system. This component includes three subcomponents: reforming the business inspections system; supporting SMEs to improve export readiness; and supporting international recognition of NQI. Finally, the second component is the project implementation and coordination support. This component will help to ensure effective implementation of all project components. This component will finance goods, services, training, and operating costs to support the implementation and coordination support for the project, inter alia by financing: (a) consultants to support project management, fiduciary, and M&E functions for the project; (b) capacity building for PIU; and (c) equipment and operating costs necessary for the project implementation.
To support product certification for export markets, strengthen the capacity of export-oriented firms and reduce the cost of business inspections.

title.narrative: Number of inspection visits per firm each year

comment.narrative: The Bank and PIU are coordinating with the IFC who has contracted a firm to measure this indicator. The reform has not been fully implemented yet. The surveys conducted confirm 1.59 visits in 2022 and 2.4 in 2021. [EI1] [BQ2] The reform (introduction of e-inspector system) has not been fully implemented yet, but the number of inspection visits reduced as risk-based methodology is applied as prescribed by the new Law on Inspections

title.narrative: Number of inspection visits per firm each year
Number of inspection visits per firm each year

comment.narrative: <p><em>The surveys conducted confirm 2.4 visits per firm in 2021, 1.59 visits in 2022, and 1.96 visits in January–August 2023 (extrapolated to 2.93 for the whole duration of 2023). The number of inspection visits reduced as risk-based methodology is applied as prescribed by the new Law on Inspections.</em></p>

title.narrative: Number of inspectorates within government body (Number)

comment.narrative: List of inspectorates prescribed by the Law on Inspection as provided by GIO. It includes 29 inspectorates but only 24 of them are subject of the reform. This consolidation is not fully implemented yet, pending substantial legal reform and amendments to sectoral/process laws. Consultants will help GIO outline/prepare for this reform and consolidation, but it is not likely to be adopted  by the Parliament and implemented by the Project end date to reach the target of 15.

Reduction in annual inspection compliance cost per business

comment.narrative: Annual inspection compliance cost per business (including staff time, travel and other costs but not fines) was €220 in 2010 (baseline), and reduced to €148.8 in 2021 and €52.6 euros in 2022. The reduction mostly comes from the reduction of numbe of inspection visits per year to companies as risk-based methodology is applied as prescribed by the new Law on inspections.

comment.narrative: <p><em>Annual inspection compliance cost per business (including staff time, travel and other costs but not fines) was EUR220 in 2010 (baseline), and reduced to EUR148.8 in 2021, EUR62.89 in 2022, and EUR44.8 in 2023 (extrapolation from EUR29.2 in January–August 2023). Share of beneficiaries of the matching grants program that increase their export value relative to firms of similar size in same sector

comment.narrative:
<p><em>8 out the 25 beneficiaries in round 1 increased their exports relative to comparator firms by year 3 (2022) after receiving the grant. </em></p>

<p><em>The analysis could not be performed for the beneficiaries in the second round as they completed their investments in 2023, and the impact on the exports could be felt at least year or two later. Furthermore, official data for comparator firms for 2023 was not available by the time of the ICR. In absence of official data, the impact of the second round of the MGP on the export of the beneficiary MSMEs was further confirmed through the self reporting instrument applied in ?mid-2023 by the grnt implementing entity. The survey showed that the investments in the certifications, equipment, and advisory services contributed to the overall increase of the exports of the 102 export-oriented beneficiary companies by 6.5 percent within a year of signing the grant agreements and before the activities were fully completed. The implementing entity for the second round collected baseline data on exports for 2021 (€51.1 million) and final data for 2022 (€54.45 million), even though most of the activities continued implementation in 2023. The exports should be even higher once the full effects from these investments begin to emerge. The 35 non-exporters supported through the grant program will most likely begin to export in the coming years, as the export strategies and initial contacts with foreign buyers supported through this project begin to materialize into sales. The project’s impact was most notable among the microenterprises, whose exports rose by 47 percent year-on-year, although they had a lower starting point of about EUR88,000 export per company—but fully justifying the decision to include them in the second round of grants. The inrease was more gradual among small firms (4.5 percent) and medium firms (5.7 percent), who were already established exporters with average annual exports of EUR421,000 and EUR1.1 million, respectively.??????? </em></p>
